author: John T. Morse Jr.
claims: The fourteenth day of April was Friday, Good Friday.
Some religious persons believed that if the President had not been at the theatre on that sacred day, the tragedy might have been avoided.
Others noted the coincidence that the fatal shot was fired on the anniversary of the crucifixion of Jesus Christ.
General Grant and his wife were invited by the President to attend the play but could not due to prior engagements.
The President appeared in good spirits on the afternoon of the assassination, which his wife found reminiscent of the period before their son Willie's death.
The President entered his box at the theatre around nine o'clock in the evening.
The President was accompanied by his wife, Major Rathbone, and another lady.
The box was decorated with an American flag.
The door from the corridor to the vestibule was rigged with a wooden stick to be fastened from the inside.
A hole had been cut in the door leading from the vestibule into the box, allowing observation of the occupants.
George A. Atzerodt was an accomplice of Booth and was tried and condemned.
The assassination plot of 1861 is mentioned, as well as threats during Lincoln's term of office.
The successful plot of 1865 resulted in Booth's death and the trial and punishment of other involved individuals.
General Grant was unable to accept Lincoln's invitation to the theatre on the evening of the assassination due to personal engagements.

temporal_details.time: around nine o'clock in the evening
